findings.issue: Decision 3 introduces `data-group-container` specifically to avoid a `data-group-id` collision between the board wrapper and the group body, and Task 9 is explicitly tasked with re-pointing E2E locators that currently find popup group rows via `filter({ hasText: groupLabel })` — text that disappears once the title becomes an input value (code-research U2, category А1, ~30 call sites across 0006/0007/0008 specs). But no task or decision defines what stable identifier Task 9 should use for a *popup row* instead. Task 8 (same wave) owns the popup markup change and does not list adding a row-level identifying attribute among its deliverables. If an implementer reaches for `data-group-id` on the popup row (the obvious name), it collides with the existing `data-group-id` on the board's group body while the popup is open (board stays mounted under the modal overlay) — reproducing, inside the popup, exactly the strict-mode-violation / silent-wrong-element failure mode Decision 3 was written to prevent for the board wrapper. This is a real gap in wave-3 task decomposition: Task 8 and Task 9 share an implicit contract that is never written down.
findings.fix: Extend Decision 3 (or add a Decision) to specify a distinct attribute for popup group rows, e.g. `data-group-row="<id>"`, and add it explicitly to Task 8's file list/description so Task 9 has a defined target to migrate onto before it starts.

findings.issue: CSS `order` (Decision 1) deliberately leaves DOM order, tab order and screen-reader reading order unchanged while visual order becomes user-configurable — confirmed explicitly in the code-research's own empirical probe (U1, point 1). The tech-spec never mentions this trade-off anywhere (Solution, Decisions, Risks). The project already applies `role="button"`/`tabindex="0"` on interactive elements (TaskCard, CollapsibleGroup header), showing some existing keyboard-accessibility awareness, so a keyboard user who reorders 'In Progress' to the top will still Tab through groups in the original backlog→...→completed sequence with no acknowledgment of the mismatch.
findings.fix: Not necessarily a blocker for an Obsidian desktop plugin, but should be named as an accepted limitation next to the other documented risks, rather than left unaddressed.

findings.issue: `Group.title` and `Board.title` are distinct interface fields, but inside `BoardSettingsPopup.svelte` the existing local variable for the board's title is already named `title` (L12). The code-research flagged this ambiguity (Problem #10) but the tech-spec's Data Models / task descriptions never resolve it with a concrete naming convention for the per-group title state (e.g. `groupTitles`, `titleDrafts`).
findings.fix: State the local variable name for per-group title editing state in the tech-spec (or leave it to task execution, but flag it so the reviewer checks for the collision) to avoid an implementer accidentally shadowing or misnaming board vs. group title state.

findings.issue: Keeping the six literal `{#if}` blocks (Decision 1) and applying order purely via CSS locks `BoardLayout.svelte` further into a fixed-six-groups shape. This is consistent with the user-spec's explicit non-goal ("the set of groups stays fixed") and is a reasonable, well-justified trade-off for this feature — but it is worth naming explicitly as accepted technical debt: any future feature that needs a variable number of groups (add/remove) will have to redo this exact markup as a keyed `{#each}` and re-verify the SortableJS survival property that Decision 1 relies on today.
findings.fix: No action needed now; optionally note in the Risks table as a forward-looking constraint for anyone scoping a future 'custom groups' feature.

summary: The central decision (CSS `order` on stable wrappers instead of a keyed `{#each}`) is sound, well-verified against the actual grid CSS and against feature 0007's half/half-alone packing rule, and correctly removes the SortableJS-recreation risk; data model, migration, and internal contract changes (`updateBoard`, `onSave`) follow existing per-board-setting conventions closely with no backward-compatibility issues. One real gap needs fixing before implementation: Task 8 (popup UI) and Task 9 (E2E locator migration) share an unwritten dependency on a stable popup-row identifier, and without one the fix risks reintroducing the exact `data-group-id` collision Decision 3 already solved for the board wrapper.
